controls.reason: Both generic prompt profiles failed requested script; longer prompt also corrupted speech text. Parent explicitly rejected both profiles and canceled unnecessary control matrix rather than considering them for production. No prompt-safety or non-speech rejection claim is made.

findings: All tested Punjabi profiles remain Latin-script: canonical Basegreedy, beam3, minimalGurmukhi-label+beam3, and longer genericGurmukhi seed.
Longer generic Gurmukhi prior-transcript seed also produces unrelatedEnglish/mixed-script text; reject the prompt.
Both Urdu examples have exactly unchanged WER under Basebeam3 vs Basegreedy (36.36% and70%). CER moves13.10%vs14.48% on one clip and24.69%vs23.46% on the other.
Beam3 retains the source numeral word `چھے` in UR1 but many surrounding words remain incorrect; this isolated repair is not sufficient for a production decoder change.
No beam/prompt setting is recommended; language-specific trained models require separate evaluation.
limits: Actual Linux x86_64 JNI/Whisper/model inference; no Android microphone, phone, TTS or physical2GB acceptance.
Punjabi reference is Gurmukhi while hypotheses are Latin; cross-script WER/CER are mismatch indicators, not fluent-speaker linguistic accuracy.
All timings are shared-host observations with at most4inference threads across two agents. Generic host SIMD options were OFF. No Android/NEON speed prediction.
Initial prompts condition prior text; they are not binding script instructions.
Returned text-token mean logp is instrumentation only and differs from internal sequence average/no-speech rules.
